issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (leading underscore), but the template repository and the solution repository define and use `make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (no underscore). This name mismatch is a structural inconsistency in the API students are expected to implement: students following the problem statement may implement `_make_y_state` while the provided template, tests, and reference solution expect `make_y_state`, causing confusion or test failures.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the function name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement to request `make_y_state(...)` (no leading underscore) so it matches the template and solution, or (B) rename the function in the template and solution to `_make_y_state(...)` and update tests accordingly. Prefer option (A) to match common public function naming in the template and reference solution.

issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_make_y_state` (leading underscore), while both the template and the reference solution define and use `make_y_state` (no underscore). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity (the routine that prepares a noisy |Y> resource state) creates a direct mapping problem: students reading the problem will look for `_make_y_state` but the starter code exposes `make_y_state`, and automated tests / the solution expect `make_y_state`. This can cause students to implement the wrong symbol or be confused about which name the autograder will check.
issues.suggested_fix: Use the same identifier in all artifacts. Replace `_make_y_state` in the problem statement with `make_y_state` (no leading underscore) so it matches the template and solution. Alternatively, if the intent was to mark the helper as private, rename the template and solution functions to `_make_y_state` and update tests accordingly — but the simpler fix is to change the problem text to refer to `make_y_state`.
